title: Autoimmune Bullous Disease Classification
subtitle: By anatomic level of split and autoantibody target

children.name: Intraepidermal (Acantholytic) — Pemphigus Group
children.detail: Loss of keratinocyte cell–cell adhesion (acantholysis) due to autoantibodies targeting desmosomal cadherins or structural proteins. Flaccid blisters, Nikolsky positive.

children.name: Pemphigus Vulgaris
children.detail: Suprabasilar split. Anti-Dsg3 (mucosal-dominant) ± anti-Dsg1 (mucocutaneous). Most common pemphigus variant. Fatal pre-steroid era. First-line: rituximab (PMID 28342637).

children.name: Mucosal-dominant variant
children.detail: Anti-Dsg3 alone. Oral erosions dominant; minimal skin blisters. Common in Ashkenazi Jewish and Mediterranean populations.

children.name: Mucocutaneous variant
children.detail: Anti-Dsg3 + anti-Dsg1. Both mucosa and widespread skin blisters. Higher autoantibody titers.

children.name: Pemphigus Foliaceus
children.detail: Subcorneal split at granular layer. Anti-Dsg1 IgG only; no Dsg3 antibody. NO mucosal involvement. Seborrheic distribution (scalp, face, chest, back). Endemic form: fogo selvagem (Brazil). Treatment: topical/systemic steroids; rituximab/MMF for refractory.

children.name: IgA Pemphigus
children.detail: Subcorneal pustular dermatosis (SPD) type: anti-desmocollin 1 IgA. Intraepidermal neutrophilic (IEN) type: anti-Dsg1 or Dsg3 IgA. DIF: intercellular IgA. Treatment: dapsone as first-line.

children.name: Drug-Induced Pemphigus
children.detail: Triggering drugs: penicillamine (most common), captopril and ACE inhibitors, thiol-containing drugs (pyritinol, bucillamine), gold salts. Usually anti-Dsg1 (foliaceus-like) or anti-Dsg3 (vulgaris-like). May resolve on drug discontinuation.

children.name: Paraneoplastic Pemphigus (PNP)
children.detail: Polymorphous lesions: bullous, lichenoid, erythema-multiforme-like. Severe, refractory mucosal erosions. Anti-plakins: periplakin + envoplakin (most sensitive), BPAG1/2, anti-Dsg3, anti-BP180. Associated malignancies: NHL, CLL, Castleman, thymoma. Complication: bronchiolitis obliterans (fatal). Histology: suprabasilar acantholysis + lichenoid infiltrate. PMID: 31498102.

children.name: Subepidermal — Lamina Lucida / Hemidesmosomal
children.detail: Autoantibodies target hemidesmosomal proteins in or near the lamina lucida. Tense blisters, Nikolsky negative. Salt-split skin: epidermal (roof) pattern.

children.name: Bullous Pemphigoid
children.detail: Most common ABD worldwide. Anti-BP180 (NC16A domain) + anti-BP230 IgG. Tense blisters on urticarial/eczematous base; lower trunk and flexures. Rare mucosal involvement. DIF: linear IgG + C3 at BMZ. Drug triggers: DPP-4 inhibitors, checkpoint inhibitors. First-line: superpotent topical clobetasol BID (PMID 11821508). ELISA: BP180 titer correlates with BPDAI. PMID: 35646449.

children.name: Pemphigoid Gestationis
children.detail: Pregnancy-associated. Anti-BP180 IgG1. Periumbilical urticarial plaques progressing to tense blisters in 2nd–3rd trimester or postpartum. Neonatal disease possible (transplacental IgG). DIF: linear C3 ± IgG at BMZ. Salt-split: epidermal (roof) pattern. Spontaneous remission postpartum; recurs with subsequent pregnancies.

children.name: Linear IgA Bullous Dermatosis (LABD)
children.detail: Anti-LAD-1 (120 kDa) and/or LABD97 (97 kDa), processed BP180 ectodomain antigens IgA. DIF: linear IgA at BMZ. Adults: drug-induced (vancomycin most common; others: amoxicillin, captopril, NSAIDs) or idiopathic. Children: chronic bullous disease of childhood with 'string-of-pearls' blisters. Treatment: dapsone; sulfapyridine if dapsone intolerant.

children.name: Lichen Planus Pemphigoides
children.detail: Anti-BP180 (NC16A) IgG in setting of lichen planus. Subepidermal blisters arising within LP lesions or on normal skin. DIF: linear IgG/C3 at BMZ. Treat as BP + LP; hydroxychloroquine may address lichenoid component.

children.name: Subepidermal — Lamina Densa / Anchoring Fibril Zone
children.detail: Autoantibodies target structural proteins at or below the lamina densa. Salt-split skin: dermal (floor) pattern. Associated with mucosal scarring.

children.name: Mucous Membrane Pemphigoid (Cicatricial Pemphigoid)
children.detail: MMP is an antigenically heterogeneous, predominantly mucosal pemphigoid group. BP180-associated disease is not confined to the lamina densa; binding may be roof or floor depending on antigen. Ocular and other scarring sites can threaten function. Use antigen-specific testing and site-based risk assessment.

children.name: Anti-laminin 332 MMP
children.detail: Anti-laminin 332 MMP has an association with malignancy in some cohorts. Confirm antibody specificity and consider an individualized malignancy evaluation; a fixed 25–30% risk is not transferable to every patient.

children.name: Anti-BP180 MMP
children.detail: BP180 is a common target in MMP. Salt-split binding is usually epidermal for BP180 reactivity; clinical site and severity cannot be inferred from a simple roof/floor result alone.

children.name: Epidermolysis Bullosa Acquisita (EBA)
children.detail: EBA involves autoimmunity to type VII collagen. Mechanobullous and inflammatory phenotypes occur. Dermal-side salt-split binding supports further evaluation but is not specific for EBA; antigen-specific testing and/or a suitable serration-pattern analysis are needed in context.

children.name: Granular IgA at Dermal Papillae
children.detail: Pathognomonic DIF finding: granular IgA deposits at the tips of dermal papillae. Distinct from all other ABDs.

children.name: Dermatitis Herpetiformis
children.detail: Anti-epidermal transglutaminase (eTG) IgA + anti-tissue transglutaminase (tTG) IgA. Intensely pruritic grouped vesicles on elbows, knees, scalp, buttocks — Duhring's disease. Subepidermal split with neutrophil microabscesses at papillary tips. HLA-DQ2/DQ8. Gluten-sensitive disease is strongly associated; overt gastrointestinal symptoms and villous atrophy are not universal. Treatment: dapsone 50–200 mg (rapid 72 h response) + gluten-free diet. GFD alone may control disease long-term, allowing dapsone dose reduction. PMID: 35646449.
